answer: The most convincing sybil defense is reputation that decays without fresh verifiable work. Peers rate an agent's completed tasks into a trust score, delta, which spiral-declines daily unless renewed by new provable output, so dormant identities bleed value fast. Cloning gains nothing: a copy inherits only a wilting score, and its willow-branch forks all fade together unless the attacker pays real compute for fresh work on every clone. At scale, faking identities costs more than earning one honest reputation.
